core_obligations: Produce the short exact sequence of tensor products (proof lines 3106-3114): by the cited flatness criterion, the flatness of the terms of K_3^bullet makes 0 -> Tot(L^bullet tensor K_1^bullet) -> Tot(L^bullet tensor K_2^bullet) -> Tot(L^bullet tensor K_3^bullet) -> 0 short exact for every complex L^bullet.

Use the long exact cohomology sequence (proof lines 3115-3116): if two of the three total tensor products are acyclic then so is the third, since a short exact sequence of complexes propagates acyclicity in two out of three positions.
Conclude (proof line 3116): since this holds for every complex L^bullet, K-flatness is two out of three for the given short exact sequence.
proof_roadmap: Use flatness of the terms of the third complex to get a short exact sequence of total tensor products.
Apply the long exact cohomology sequence to propagate acyclicity two out of three.
Quantify over all test complexes to obtain the K-flatness statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the two out of three property for K-flatness to a short exact sequence of complexes whose third complex has flat terms (statement lines 3096-3103). The proof replaces the distinguished triangle of the companion lemma by a short exact sequence: flatness of the terms of K_3^bullet is what makes the sequence of total tensor products short exact for every test complex L^bullet (proof lines 3106-3114), after which acyclicity propagates two out of three through the long exact cohomology sequence and K-flatness follows by quantifying over L^bullet (proof lines 3115-3116). The non-formal content is the identification of the exactness hypothesis with flatness of the terms. The claim is H2: one reduction using a cited flatness criterion.
